title: Find a Product
real_world_story: A customer searches for a product using its product ID. The product catalog is currently stored as an unsorted list of product IDs. Determine whether the requested product exists in the catalog.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Product IDs currently stored in the catalog
real_world_connection.target_represents: Product ID requested by the customer
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Searching through the catalog to locate a product

problem_statement: Given an array of product IDs and a target product ID, determine whether the target product exists in the catalog. Return the index of the product if it exists; otherwise return -1.
task: Search the product catalog and return the index of the requested product.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of products. The second line contains N integers representing product IDs. The third line contains an integer target representing the product ID to search for.
output_format: Print the zero-based index of the target product if it exists. Otherwise, print -1.

examples.explanation: Product ID 305 is present at index 2.
Product ID 700 does not exist in the catalog.

expected_algorithm.name: Linear Search
expected_algorithm.reason: The product IDs are not guaranteed to be sorted, so each product may need to be checked sequentially.

hint: Compare each product ID with the target ID.
Stop when the target is found.
real_world_takeaway: A straightforward search can be sufficient for small or unsorted datasets, but repeatedly scanning a very large catalog can become expensive.
